text:
adele: Heads-up: CI is red on main, typecheck/format gate. Seems intermittent — my local `pre-commit run --all-files` is green. Anybody else seeing noisy mypy/pyright + eslint failures on pushes?

chris: Saw the same. CI job `typecheck-and-lint` failed on two different runs for different PRs. Logs show a pyright TS error and a mypy Optional error on different files.

juan: Linking one of the failing jobs: https://ci.internal.redwood/1234 — the pyright error looks like it started after the TS -> pybind stub change in #4821.

maya: I retried the same job twice, first run failed, rerun passed. Could be cache-related or flaky cache invalidation.

adele: Repro steps I tried: checkout main @ abcdef1, run `tox -e typecheck` inside container `registry/redwood/py-typecheck:prod-2026-03-01`, first run passes, second run fails (identical env).

sam: @devops-oncall can you kick off a bisect across the last ~20 commits for the typecheck job? If it's a cache flake we should catch the commit that made the job non-deterministic.

devops-oncall: Starting bisect now. Plan: binary search between commit abcdef1 (known-good from yesterday) and HEAD (bad). Will post intermediate commit SHAs and results here.

ci-bot: bisect: queued job #bisect-1923456789-1 for commit 889ab2c.

ci-bot: bisect: job #bisect-1923456789-1 FAILED — mypy Optional check error at `server/utils/serialization.py:142`.

devops-oncall: Running next midpoint commit 99c0d5a...

ci-bot: bisect: job #bisect-1923456789-2 PASSED.

chris: OK that narrows to commits between 99c0d5a and 889ab2c. Any recent changes touching kvcache stubs or typing?

juan: There was a small refactor in #4890 that relaxed a typed dict and added a `# type: ignore` previously. I wonder if the change to the pyright stub generator in #4922 could cause intermittent ordering in generated stubs (flaky).

maya: FYI eslint failures are a separate pattern — some transient max-len hits on generated proto files. We might need to exclude generated code from lint or re-run the generator with stable line wrapping.

devops-oncall: Continuing bisect: testing commit d4f3b77...

ci-bot: bisect: job #bisect-1923456789-3 FAILED (mypy error same as first failure).

devops-oncall: Bisect narrowed: offending change is in commit d4f3b77 (author: juan) — it touches `tools/pystubgen` and `server/kvcache/__init__.py`.

juan: Oof — that was the pybind stub ordering fix. My change collapsed a dict iteration which may have changed stable ordering of generated stubs. I'll open an immediate PR to add deterministic sorting in the generator.

adele: Thanks. For short-term mitigation: can we mark generated stubs as `# type: ignore` or add them to excluded paths in mypy config? We should avoid ignoring everything though.

chris: Quick patch: add `generated/**/*.py` to mypy `exclude` in `pyproject.toml` and add eslint ignore for `generated/**` — low risk and buys time. I'll draft the PR.

maya: I'll follow up on the eslint proto wrapping; generator can enforce 80/100 char wrapping after sorting.

devops-oncall: After revert-ish fix, I re-ran the gate on HEAD — job passed twice in a row.

ci-bot: rerun: `typecheck-and-lint` on HEAD — PASSED.

adele: Awesome. Juan, please put up the deterministic-sort PR and link here. Also include a unit test that ensures generator output is stable across runs.

juan: Will do. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/r/4955 — adds sorted iteration + test + changelog.

sam: Minor ask: can the bisect tooling include an option to auto-rerun flaky jobs twice before declaring PASS/FAIL? Would reduce noise.

devops-oncall: Good idea. Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-1287 to add `--flaky-retries` to bisect runner.

chris: TL;DR: root cause = non-deterministic stubgen output (commit d4f3b77). Short-term: exclude generated from mypy/eslint; Long-term: deterministic generator + test + bisect tooling improvements.

adele: Nice triage everyone. Will mark the incident as resolved once PR 4955 is merged and infra ticket created. :thumbsup:
